claims.summary: The observed Codex base instructions say not to create a commit or branch unless explicitly requested.
Claude Code documents a headless example that reviews staged changes with git diff, log, status, and commit permissions.
Claude Code documents built-in commit and pull-request instructions, a git status snapshot, configurable attribution, permissions, and hooks.
Conventional Commits 1.0.0 defines type, optional scope, description, optional body, and footer structure.
The commit skill does not create a commit until the user explicitly requests one.
Only intended paths are staged; unrelated staged, unstaged, and untracked changes are preserved.
The staged diff is re-reviewed and existing Git hooks run normally; --no-verify is not used without a separate explicit request.
Amend, push, tag, and branch creation require separate explicit requests.
After a commit, the skill reports and verifies the commit SHA, show output, status, and remaining changes.
Local --version commands observed codex-cli 0.146.0 and Claude Code 2.1.220 on 2026-08-03. No same-fixture product behavior result is recorded in Phase 1.

unsupported_guarantees.summary: Codex and Claude Code are not claimed to use identical internal commit algorithms or to produce identical commits.
Undocumented staging, message-selection, hook, or attribution algorithms are not product guarantees.
Harness safety policy is not represented as behavior guaranteed by either product.
No official or third-party commit skill, prompt, plugin file, or runtime implementation is imported.
An observed source change never updates the contract or commit skill automatically.
